name: Argentina

facts.religion: Catholic about 63%, growing evangelical and non-religious shares

snapshot: Javier Milei's chainsaw austerity crushed inflation and won him a labour reform in 2026, but factories and shops are shrinking and jobs are now the top worry.
culture: Argentina is football: Maradona is close to a saint, and Messi's 2022 World Cup brought millions onto the streets. Tango was born in Buenos Aires' port neighbourhoods in the late 1800s. Sunday asado, mate passed around a circle, and Italian and Spanish immigrant roots shape daily life. Borges and Cortázar gave Argentina a towering literary tradition.
society: A century ago one of the world's richest countries, Argentina has since defaulted nine times. Poverty rose above 50 percent in early 2024 before falling as inflation eased. Peronism, the movement founded by Juan Perón, still shapes unions and politics. The pampas make it a farm superpower in beef, soy and wheat, and Vaca Muerta shale is a new oil frontier.
situation: A century ago Argentina was one of the ten richest countries on Earth. Since then it has defaulted on its debt nine times and lived through hyperinflation, and by 2023 prices were rising more than 200 percent a year. Voters responded by electing Javier Milei, a wild-haired libertarian economist who campaigned with a chainsaw and called himself an "anarcho-capitalist." Few expected him to last. In 2026 he looked stronger than ever.

Inflation fell from 211 percent in 2023 to 31.5 percent in 2025, the economy grew 4.4 percent, and Argentina posted a budget surplus for two years running for the first time since 2008 (AFP via Buenos Aires Times). His party's win in the October 2025 midterms gave him enough allies in Congress to pass a long-blocked labour reform early this year, loosening hiring and firing rules in a country where union power is legendary (Friedrich Naumann Foundation). On 1 March he declared 2026 the "year of Argentine greatness" and laid out 90 more reforms to "remake" the country for the next 50 years, pausing to call opposition lawmakers "thieves" and "parasites" (Berliner Zeitung). The cost is real. Growth has come from farming and finance while manufacturing and retail, the biggest employers, have shrunk, and jobs and wages have replaced inflation as Argentines' top worry. Milei is closely aligned with Trump, whose government backed him with a financial lifeline in 2025. On the pitch, Argentina reached the World Cup final in July and lost to Spain in extra time.
power: A federal presidential republic. The president is directly elected for four years with one consecutive re-election; Congress has a Senate and a Chamber of Deputies, half of which is renewed every two years. The 23 provinces have strong governors who often decide whether presidents can pass laws.
holders: President Javier Milei (La Libertad Avanza), in office since December 2023.
